happeningTypes.name: Generate a positive personal future episode and display its event cue during a specified choice task
happeningTypes.description: Ask a participant to elaborate a realistic positive future event and display a cue to that event during a specified decision. Valence, event timing and cue content are operation parameters; identity promises no efficacy, patience, trait change or practitioner permission.
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, emotional burden, accessibility, truthful task framing and actor/context assessment required; no financial or clinical recommendation.

happeningTypes.name: Preselect a specified option while permitting explicit switching or decline
happeningTypes.description: Designate a particular option as initially selected in a bounded choice interface, with declared alternatives and switching/declining procedure. No preference change, efficacy, endorsement, permission or welfare benefit is implied.
happeningTypes.constraints: Informed consent, transparency, accessibility, genuine alternatives, legal/ethical review, conflicts of interest and choice autonomy require independent assessment. No recommendation ranking.

assertions.scope: Positive personal future-episode cue displayed during specified hypothetical monetary intertemporal choices in studied adults; no uncued persistence or general trait claim. Exact canonical discount-rate/curve specification remains unresolved.
assertions.measurement: Rung2019 adjusting-amount indifference points at6months/1year (E1), not uniquely identified full discount curve or beta. LEVEL of a rate construct is not its temporal derivative.
assertions.timing: Immediate cue-present task; future-event delay not onset/persistence of an intervention effect.
assertions.mechanism: Episodic prospection/cue salience may alter currently represented outcomes; temporal-horizon mediation and demand-free process not established.
assertions.risk: Convenience samples, hypothetical rewards, cue demands, measurement-model dependence and no clinical/financial benefit inference.
assertions.rationale: Randomized local choice differences and syntheses support bounded reduced discounting, but exact Driver rate specification and operation heterogeneity prevent a uniform signed effect. Preserve positive results and cue-absent/neutral-content nondetection rather than universal efficacy.

assertions.scope: Specified preselected option versus active-choice/alternative-default comparator in declared choice domain; independent subjective preference measure needed.
assertions.measurement: Behavioral uptake is not necessarily changed preference; switching costs, inertia, endorsement and endowment require separation.
assertions.timing: At choice; no assumed preference persistence or reversal lag.
assertions.mechanism: Designation can change ease or inferred endorsement without changing latent valuation.
assertions.risk: Autonomy, coercion, accessibility and conflicts of interest; no automatic welfare or practitioner permission.
assertions.rationale: Meta-analysis strongly supports heterogeneous choice effects, including null/negative cases, but exact subjective-preference alignment is unresolved. No universal direction assigned to latent Driver.

findings.sample: Two experiments; exact analyzed N not extracted
findings.population: US MTurk adults19–60; exclusions for prior EFT/task attention specified
findings.context: US MTurk adults19–60; exclusions for prior EFT/task attention specified
findings.exposure: Generate positive realistic future events plus displayed event cues
findings.comparator: Recent positive-event thinking with cues; randomized cue-presence design
findings.result: Cue-present future thinking reduced local discounting relative to recent-event control; relevant event content matters.
findings.limitations: Local choice-derived measure, not whole rate/curve or present-beta identification. No enduring trait, welfare or actual future spending claim.

findings.result: No reduction detected without relevant event cues; delay-only/demand cues not sufficient.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE exact cue-present identity; boundary evidence, not equivalence or proof no effect at all delays. Same experiment contribution.

findings.measurement: Future Time Perspective maximum/median event extension
findings.result: Future horizon did not expand; recent-event control shortened horizon, challenging mediation interpretation.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE PSY-089 direct target; control change and incompatible mediation regressions do not identify a causal pathway. Nondetection not equality.

findings.result: Average reduced discounting; positive future content more favorable, neutral/negative contrast near zero; task/control moderators.
findings.limitations: Operation, valence and measurement vary; near-zero average is not equivalence. Overlaps Rosch and primary EFT reports, not independent replication.

findings.measurement: Discounting, hypothetical cigarette demand, craving and hypothesis awareness
findings.result: Reduced discounting and cigarette-demand intensity; no elasticity/craving effect. Adjusted awareness did not eliminate discounting result.
findings.limitations: Demand-awareness coding/adjustment cannot prove all expectancy bias absent. Cigarette outcomes OUTSIDE PSY-089; same study outcomes not replications.

findings.population: Consumer, environmental and other choice domains
findings.context: Consumer, environmental and other choice domains
findings.result: Positive average default-choice effect; substantial heterogeneity across domains and mechanisms.
findings.limitations: Uptake not independent subjective preference; coded ease/endorsement/endowment not identified mediator. Includes canonical Johnson/Goldstein work.

findings.result: Several included studies report no detected default effect.
findings.limitations: No equivalence inference; no null latent-preference claim. Same review, not additional independent synthesis.

findings.population: Specific review settings, not universal reversal
findings.context: Specific review settings, not universal reversal
findings.result: Two included studies show effects opposite the common default-uptake direction.
findings.limitations: Contrary to universal uptake increase, not proof of universal preference decrease. Context-specific primary extraction remains needed.
